chunks: 3474 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about a man who wanted to free a slave of his, while his master had been taking from him a yearly levy that he had imposed on him, and the master was satisfied with that from him. Then the slave acquired wealth in his trade besides what he used to give his master from the levy. So he said: “When he has paid to his master what he had imposed upon him, then whatever he earns after the obligation belongs to the slave.”

He said: Then Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: “Has not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed obligations upon the servants, and when they perform them for Him, He does not ask them about what is beyond them?”
I said to him: “Then may the slave give charity from what he earned and be emancipated after the obligation that he pays to his master?” He said: “Yes, and the reward of that is for him.”

I said: “If he frees a slave from what he had earned apart from the obligation, to whom does the walaʾ of the emancipated one belong?” He said: “He goes and affiliates himself with whomever he wishes, and when someone guarantees his liability and blood-money responsibility, he becomes his mawla and inherits from him.”

I said to him: “Did not the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say: ‘The walaʾ belongs to the one who emancipates’?” He said: “This is a saʾibah; his walaʾ does not belong to a slave like him.”

I said: “If the slave who emancipated him guarantees his liability and incident, would that bind him, and would he become his mawla and inherit from him?” He said: “That is not permissible. A slave does not inherit from a free person.”

key_terms.جَرِيرَتَهُ: his liability for offenses or obligations
key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: a freed person not attached by walaʾ to the emancipating slave
key_terms.ضَرِيبَةً: a fixed levy or payment imposed by the master
key_terms.وَلَاءُ: the bond of patronage or allegiance linked to manumission
key_terms.يَتَصَدَّقَ: to give charity from one’s earnings
key_terms.ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ: the required obligation that must be paid first

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about a slave’s earnings, charity, manumission, and walaʾ after paying an agreed levy to his master?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings concerning a slave who pays a fixed annual levy to his master and then earns additional wealth through trade. It states that earnings beyond the imposed obligation belong to the slave, allowing him to give charity and even emancipate another slave, while clarifying that walaʾ and inheritance do not accrue to a slave over a free person.
